title: The Covenant of Grace
definition: The Covenant of Grace is God's gracious saving arrangement by which He promises life and redemption through Christ to sinners.
summary: The Covenant of Grace describes God's unified plan to save sinners through Christ across redemptive history.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the mediator and fulfillment of God's covenant promises.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
The covenant of grace describes God's saving commitment to redeem sinners through His promised mercy. Scripture unfolds one gracious purpose that centers on Christ and reaches His people by faith.

This doctrine helps believers see that salvation is not an emergency reaction by God. From promise to fulfillment, God is faithful to save by grace.

Jesus is the mediator and fulfillment of God's gracious covenant purpose. All the promises of God find their yes in Him.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Scattered Bible stories can feel disconnected. The covenant of grace shows the unity of God's saving work and helps believers read Scripture as one unfolding story of redemption in Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Read the Bible looking for God's faithful promise and fulfillment in Christ. Let His covenant mercy strengthen trust when circumstances feel unstable, and teach salvation as God's gracious work from beginning to end.
